newsitem.title: USA: Economists divided whether Fed will add reserves.
newsitem.headline: Economists divided whether Fed will add reserves.

text.p: Economists were divided on whether the Federal Reserve would stay out of or add reserves to the banking system on Friday.

"The Fed should be able to stay out of the market today and may well be sidelined until settlement day next Wednesday. The $7.0 billion 14-day fixed RP (repurchase agreement) arranged Monday will stay in effect through the end of the (current maintenance) period and the settlement of yesterday's bill pass will provide an additional $4.0 billion beginning today," said Marc Wanshel, economist at Morgan Guaranty Trust Co.

However, economists at UBS Securities Inc said that even after Thursday's bill pass and large overnight system, the Fed still faced a sizable $5.0 billion daily add need in the remaining six days of the current maintenance period.
Fed funds were trading at 5-3/8 percent, slightly below the Fed's current official target level of 5.50 percent.
